question: Does posterior-risk pair acquisition improve final mechanism prediction beyond a fixed varied-value pair design at equal acquisition cost?
primary_contrast: risk_pair minus factorial_hub_pair, paired by system
primary_gate: ratio of mean risk_pair error to mean factorial_hub_pair error below 0.80 and upper endpoint of a two-sided 95% paired t interval for risk_pair minus factorial_hub_pair below zero
secondary_context: Report risk_pair against coverage_pair, balanced_risk_pair, and the strongest fixed pair arm. No secondary test can override a failed primary gate. Report single arms and exact costs without claiming joint-action superiority.
interpretation: A primary pass supports an adaptive pair-selection advantage only in this exact synthetic binary-tree family and action menu. It does not establish a foundation-model effect. A failure leaves B unpromoted.
resource: 40 small local numerical systems; no GPU or closed-source model calls. Archive all cells and hashes even on gate failure.
limits: The factorial control concentrates four actions at motif 0 while risk can choose motifs. It matches varied pair values and total cost, but does not separately isolate motif allocation from value selection. Same simulator family as development.
forbidden: Do not alter simulator, learner, action rules, seeds, budget, endpoint, or threshold after inspecting these results
